title: Lesson 4: Building a Custom Tool: Tailored Instructions, Saved Context, Your Own Project
description: What a custom tool is, why it beats retyping the same prompt, and how tailored instructions, saved context, and a project come together into something you control.

questions.question: A custom tool holds three things. Which one supplies the examples, notes, and templates the tool consults so you stop re-explaining your department?
options: The tailored instructions, which set the standing format and tone
Your own project, which keeps all the chats in one place
The saved context, which holds reference material for the task
The review step, which checks each draft before it ships
questions.explanation: Saved context is the reference material, past examples, background notes, and templates, that the tool draws on across chats. Without it you would re-explain your world on every run.

questions.question: Once the standing instructions and reference material are saved, what does each new run of the workflow need from you?
options: The full prompt restated each time, so the tool stays aligned
A fresh copy of the background material pasted in for the tool
A new format choice each run, since the old one no longer applies
Just the fresh facts for that run, with the rest in place
questions.explanation: The saved setup carries the format, tone, and background, so the input shrinks to the new facts. That reduction is the payoff, because the decisions are made once instead of weekly.

questions.question: What does a custom tool change about the review step?
options: Nothing: it drafts faster and better shaped but still errs sometimes
It removes the review, because the saved instructions prevent errors
It moves the review inside the tool, which checks its own output
It makes the review optional for low-stakes runs only
questions.explanation: A custom tool saves the re-deciding, not the checking. The output still needs a person to confirm it before it ships, because a confident draft can still be wrong.
